## TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] S3: This show is brought to you with support from Actable, the company that helps more than 150,000 hoteliers run more efficient and profitable hotel businesses every day, at every level. See why more than 90% of the top 50 management companies in the US use Actable at actable.com. That's a c t a b l .com.
[00:24] S1: Today in this third and final episode with Hotel Equities CEO Ben Rafter, we go back to where we started with his series and that is what it takes to drive real results using technology in the hotel business today. We recorded what you're about to hear at the end of May 2026. It was interesting because shortly after we recorded at the NYU International Hospitality Investment Forum, I found leader after leader coming back to AI, turning to technology to drive profitability. But of all these presentations and panels, I found that what you're about to hear, hear with Ben, is the sharpest view and the most specific plan for driving results. That's what we get into here. We talk a bit more about AE Labs and the process that they use, and then some of the questions that owners should be asking when it comes to who is the best operating partner for them in this environment. So without further ado, let's get into it.
[01:17] S3: Hospitality. Hospitality. Hospitality. Hospitality brings people together.
[01:28] S3: This is Hospitality Daily, the show that helps you stay informed and inspired each day by the most interesting people in hospitality. My name is Josiah McKenzie, and my goal is to help you reconnect with why you work in this industry and get fired up to go out there, delight others and reach your goals. Let's get started.
[01:52] S1: What is disappointing? What's exciting or kind of where you're seeing potential today in with AI?
[01:57] S2 (Ben Rafter): So, I think we're three to five years out before AI actually tells me and tells you, this is the hotel you need to stay in for your Los Angeles business trip or your Los Angeles vacation or you know, that's not here yet. I'm a little bit surprised we're not further along in terms of consumer-facing decision making to choose your hospitality state, whether business or or leisure travel, right? Where it's it's highly advanced already is whatever 10, 15, 20 years ago we outsourced all sorts of different functions. Sometimes overseas, sometimes centrally. AI is now very rapidly and aggressively outsourcing the the outsource outsourcer, if that makes any sense.
[02:39] S1: What's an example of that?
[02:40] S2 (Ben Rafter): If we had a hundred people working on bookkeeping and finance in India two years ago, I would guess for the same productivity, we'll be able to do that with 10 people nearshore by next year.
[02:55] S1: Wow. That's a big, that's a big impact. Um, With, I mean our accuracy was never really a problem, but with better accuracy.
[03:01] S1: Amazing. Um, well and so and it all ladders up to what you mentioned at the beginning of our conversation, right? You think about kind of what is it going to take to drive NUI, to drive results for owners? You see technology as the unlock and I think you get into the specific elements of the business or the business operation. I think that's a good example of that.
[03:17] S2 (Ben Rafter): And by the way, when I reference how we started with AT Labs and all these solutions, we decompose it into all of these different opportunities. Many of those opportunities still don't have what we view as a viable solution. And so, Brian in in his role as leading AT Labs, he's out there looking for people who are developing those solutions actively, and he's reaching out to them and or they're coming to us and he's reaching out and saying, we think this is the problem. We think you might have a solution. Do you want to put it in 10 hotels? Not one, not not one where it's going to get buried, but do you want to try it in 10 hotels or actively pursuing this solution? It feels like that's how you drive results with AI. You start with a problem because I think there's still too much chasing of kind of what are the capabilities. And so you start with a problem and I think what's so cool about what you're doing with Labs at Hotel Equities is is the you have kind of like a consulting model, consulting way of looking at things in-house, right, without paying those kind of consulting retainers, but you're thinking about the problem. You're thinking about it at scale. So I mean, have a sample set where I can make a decision that this is working or it's not working, right? So again, it comes down to the kind of defendable internal capabilities of driving outperformance for owners, but you're building this all in-house.
[04:27] S2 (Ben Rafter): Yeah, and it's there's no, probably no shock to you that both Brian and I came from before hospitality came from tech consulting or finance consulting backgrounds, right? And remember as a kid, I knew people who worked for Bell Labs and worked for JPL and and worked for Caltech and um what they were doing across a different industry. All of that has sort of shaped what we're trying to do here with without trying to boil the ocean obviously, but it's sort of there's a long history of using concepts like this to make industries run more efficient or to to create innovation and and so we're we're certainly not breaking new ground. I think we're breaking a little bit of new ground in the hospitality industry. But everybody knows AI for you know, for anything that processes a zero or one, everybody knows AI works, everybody knows you can grind through mountains of data using AI. We're we're trying to take it to a a you know, the next level.
[05:23] S1: Very exciting. I was wondering if it might be worth it to talk for a few moments of the conversations that owners should be having or the selection criteria owners should be having, because I feel like there's some in the industry that say they're, you know, tech-enabled or this or that, but what you've shared is a lot. Is there any other criteria or questions you would ask owners to be asking potential management partners if they want to drive out performance from their assets? I'm curious if anything else comes to mind there.
[05:49] S2 (Ben Rafter): Everybody says they're tech-enabled, right? You we're we're going through an email migration right now and it's a little bumpier than we were expecting, so maybe we're the least tech-enabled if we can't get our email working. But what I would be asking is specific, quantifiable results. And so take hotel effectiveness and profit sword, right? I think profit sword is great at gathering and presenting the data where it would be nice for it to evolve, and it will is it proactively reaches out and says, here are the three biggest problems you have, Mr. GM, Mr. Regional Director of Ops, Mr. Revenue Manager, and you need to solve these problems within X amount of time. It it all of these systems need to be to go from presenting to actually proactively forcing somebody to make a decision. And they're getting there pretty quickly.
[06:46] S1: On the labor side, we talk pretty extensively about it, but it's the it's the same thing. In a perfect world, in a market like Texas markets, much less regulation, we have 10 hotels all right next to each other, we want to build and and there's one regional person over those 10 hotels. We want to build an ecosystem that has all 10 hotels working together to maximize the profit of all of them and then we need to convince the owners because there are at least three different ownership groups that this is actually a good thing. Yeah. I love that. I love that. But the the question I'd be answered is like, okay, you talk about technology, give me a finite example of how technology makes me make more money. Right. And show me the numbers and I feel like that you give me a lot here, Ben. I think this really represents the future and is going to, you know, put hotel equities in a in a great position. So,
[07:32] S2 (Ben Rafter): Yeah, I it's not going to be next year, the year after, but we do budgeting and things like that and it's a very big back and forth with owners. Not not so much here, because we put a lot of time and effort into this is what your budget should be, but that just real-time forecasting should be to a point where it gets incredibly accurate. And budget processes should be to a point where it's 98% automated based on data inputs. And then you're going to have an owner that says, okay, I need a bank budget or whatever, but we should be 98% accurate based on then real-time conditions with a budget on the first go round. And then something happens, we drop a bomb on Iraq or Iran or or or the state of Hermuz closes or whatever, you know, that's the real-time forecasting. You can't, you can't necessarily, you can predict that, you can't predict when or how that's going to happen. But that's we didn't even talk about that, but that to me is is a next, right? And pretty soon there should be so much science into it that an owner will be able to look at and say, my hotel is being run efficiently and here are my 10 data points as I know why.
[08:36] S1: Yeah. That's kind of where this is all going. So, Ben, it's always great to talk with you. I appreciate you making time to record.
[08:42] S3: After I recorded this conversation with Ben in May of 2026, Actable announced a suite of AI capabilities designed to help hoteliers improve hotel performance. I've linked to those announcements along with some additional resources mentioned in this conversation in the show notes if you'd like to learn more.
[09:05] S3: If you enjoyed today's conversation, I just have one favor to ask and that is to take out your phone now and text or email this episode to someone you work with or an industry friend and tell them what stood out to you. The reason I produce this show is to help you and your business. And it takes teamwork to do that. So I encourage you to move this beyond just being an idea, something you listen to, to sharing it with your team so that you can implement it in your hospitality business. And the ideas we heard today drive actual results and improvements for you. I'd also love to hear what you thought about the episode today. You can email me Josiah@hospitalitydaily.com. Hospitality Daily has become the number one podcast in hospitality. Thanks to you and the tens of thousands of hospitality providers around the world that join us each day to learn and grow together. So thank you for joining us, and if you have something to teach or share with our community, I'd love to hear from you as well. So please email me or send me a message on LinkedIn and let's talk. A few more things before we go, first, if you haven't done so already, subscribe to this podcast on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or your favorite app to stay inspired each day by actionable insights from the most interesting people in hospitality. If you'd like to listen to more conversations like the one that you just heard, visit this podcast website at podcast.hospitalitydaily.com. I spent a lot of time building out this website because I want to make it easy for you to listen to the topics and guests that you are interested in, whether that's culture and leadership or operations or technology or something else. You can browse and search the entire library of more than 650 episodes from some of the top leaders and innovators in hospitality at podcast.hospitalitydaily.com and get ideas for delighting the people around you and reaching your business and career goals. And finally, if you prefer to read a recap of these ideas each day, I'd be happy to send you my top takeaways by email. You can subscribe at hospitalitydaily.com. Thanks for listening and I'll see you here again tomorrow.

## QUOTES
- "[02:32]" "AI is now very rapidly and aggressively outsourcing the the outsource outsourcer, if that makes any sense." -> why it matters: Shows how AI replaces traditional offshored labor tasks.
- "[03:22]" "we decompose it into all of these different opportunities. Many of those opportunities still don't have what we view as a viable solution." -> why it matters: Explains their structured approach to finding missing tech solutions.
- "[06:21]" "here are the three biggest problems you have, Mr. GM, Mr. Regional Director of Ops, Mr. Revenue Manager, and you need to solve these problems within X amount of time." -> why it matters: Illustrates the shift from passive reporting to prescriptive AI.
- "[07:46]" "real-time forecasting should be to a point where it gets incredibly accurate. And budget processes should be to a point where it's 98% automated based on data inputs." -> why it matters: Outlines the future standard of automated budgeting and forecasting.
- "[08:27]" "And pretty soon there should be so much science into it that an owner will be able to look at and say, my hotel is being run efficiently and here are my 10 data points as I know why." -> why it matters: Highlights data transparency and proof of operational efficiency for owners.
